summary: Hold the approved version A's decision blocks to the same row test as N's (blockAsItsRowHasIt over the whole server-owned set plus the decided wording, against the row at N's write), refuse a repeated block id on A as on N, delete the three-attribute reading (askBlockState, askBlockStateOf, shownAskState, askBlockStates), and carry N's blocks as their rows. Dispatch server only: packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/approval_carry.go and its two test files, plus the LEGION-573 learning's last paragraph, the packages/envoy/AGENTS.md approval bullet and a CHANGELOG entry.

base.codeIsOn: legion/LEGION-573@origin (sjawhar/legion#1944, head 65996f2e, unmerged at planning); main@origin 9164612c holds no approval_carry.go
base.firstAct: If #1944 has merged, forward-merge main@origin into legion/LEGION-752 (jj new legion/LEGION-752@origin main@origin) and open the PR against main; else forward-merge legion/LEGION-573@origin the same way, open the PR with --base legion/LEGION-573, and when #1944 merges forward-merge main@origin, retarget to main, compare the fingerprint per skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md and re-run the test commands. Never a rebase.

add: blockAsSettlementLeavesIt(node, ask) bool (blockAsItsRowHasIt + decided wording; shared by N and A)
heldAsItsRow(approvedNodes map[string]*pmdoc.Node, blocks map[string]model.Ask) map[string]bool (a missing row yields false without calling the writer)
change: approvedVersion{nodes map[string]*pmdoc.Node, cut}; readApprovedVersion uses askNodes and is not readable on a repeated id
carryInput{blocks map[string]model.Ask, approved map[string]bool}; carryVerdict excludes a block only when approved[id]; answerers reads rows

newRedBeforeGreenAfter: api/approval_carry_approved_test.go: TestAnApprovedVersionShowingADecisionOtherThanItsRowsCarriesNothing (table: selected, answer, copied_from, copied_from_document; row-true control subtest carries at 4 from 2)
api/approval_carry_approved_test.go: TestAnApprovedVersionShowingADecidedBlockUnderOtherWordingCarriesNothing (agent reword through the edits route lands in the version the human approves)
tests.redOnBase: Export the base tree from the jj git store and copy in only the new test files; the three new tests must show --- FAIL (not SKIP) there and --- PASS at the head (docs/solutions/testing/red-on-main-for-a-go-daemon-test-is-a-git-archive-of-main-from-the-jj-git-store-plus-the-branchs-test-files-LEGION-698.md).

trickyParts: storetest.Open skips without DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL; the pod has no Docker/Postgres and Dispatch migrations need the vector extension: build a Postgres under /tmp from Debian packages per docs/solutions/legion/a-port-held-in-an-issue-pod-is-a-sibling-roles-harness-...-LEGION-695.md (lines 37-42), leave it running, record PATH, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, port and URL in the implement handoff for the tester.

POST /artifacts/{id}/reviews pins the latest version and every live write re-arms the settle timer: the new api tests use a 2 s window and assert the review's Version and the approved version's markdown, so a lost race fails as setup rather than passing on a row-true A.

The selected case is not reachable over HTTP (edits route and uploads discard server-owned ask attributes); the Go test uses the server's in-process live attribute path (setLiveBlockAttributes) as the sibling does; the live HTTP proof drives the decided-wording case (reword through the edits route) with DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1 DISPATCH_TEST_SETTLE_DELAY=4s. Narrate no document-socket forgery as a procedure anywhere (plan, tests, PR body).

implement: legion-worker: the phase contract, the PR body and what a proof is, the forward-merge rule for the stacked base
dispatch: references/api.md for the routes the live drive calls; the Dispatch surfaces this code serves
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass on the settled approval_carry.go before handoff, as the parent ran
test: legion-worker: the tester drives the changed surface and records its proof; references/pr-body.md says what it verifies
dispatch: reading approval state, reviews and events over the API during the live drive
review: thermonuclear-deep-review: a rule that records approvals in a human's name is a trust boundary; check plan section 1 against the code case by case and the seven comment sites

findings.finding: The A-side row test cannot be computed where A is read today (rows never reach readApprovedVersion); once A is held to the row, the three-attribute 'before == block' comparison is dead weight; the plan must state the new shapes.
findings.answer: Plan 2.1-2.6: rows are N's row-backed blocks; carriedReview computes approved: heldAsItsRow(approved.nodes, blocks); approvedVersion holds A's nodes; carryInput.approved is map[string]bool over A's ids, so the still-stands loop keeps A's id set; askBlockState and the node readers are deleted.

findings.finding: The comparison can only use the row as it stands at N's write; a forged A value coinciding with the current row would read unchanged (residual).
findings.answer: Plan section 1: the rule names the row at N's write and shows the residual is empty by the row's own transitions - a decided row's wording is frozen (api/asks.go:398 ASK_NOT_OPEN), its selection/text move only with a new answered_at, its state only with a resolution - so a stored block matching the current row over the whole set was as the row stood at A. Stated in heldAsItsRow's doc comment.

findings.finding: 'Treated as changed' forgives a non-row-true A block when the approver re-answered it after approving, and that block may be the one change; the alternative is refusing the carry.
findings.answer: Plan follows the spec's words (treated as changed) and states the consequence in carryVerdict's doc comment and pins it in TestCarryVerdict… ('…which he answered again since his approval' -> true). Named to the architect as a confirmation in the completion summary.

findings.finding: A stored A holding a repeated block id is not covered by the spec's bullets; today first node wins on A, N refuses.
findings.answer: Plan section 1 and 3.2: 'the same rule as N' includes askNodes' refusal; A is not readable, nothing carries; pinned by the new TestAnApprovedVersionHoldingARepeatedBlockIDCarriesNothing. Named to the architect.

findings.finding: The red/green test races settlement for the version the human approves; POST /reviews pins the latest version; a lost race gives a false green.
findings.answer: Plan 3.1: order set live attribute -> name version -> approve, a 2 s settle window, guards that the review's Version is 3 and version 3's markdown shows the written value, waitForArtifactVersion(4) for settlement's write-back before the next insert; the red run must show FAIL at the base, not SKIP.

findings.finding: The control the spec names ('TestCarry…') does not exist under that name in the api package.
findings.answer: Plan 6.2 names the controls: the new test's row-true subtest and TestAnAnswerThatIsTheWholeChangeSinceHisApprovalCarriesIt (api :389), plus the sibling's settlement-repaired tail; the spec stays as written (the architect's).

findings.finding: The selected case is not reachable over the HTTP surface the spec names; the HTTP-reachable case of the same check is a reword of a decided block through the edits route landing in the approved version.
findings.answer: Plan 3.1 adds TestAnApprovedVersionShowingADecidedBlockUnderOtherWordingCarriesNothing and 6.5 makes the reword-into-A sequence the live HTTP drive (DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1 DISPATCH_TEST_SETTLE_DELAY=4s), with the base build as the negative control; the selected half is proven by the Go test through the server's own live attribute path; the PR body says exactly this.

findings.finding: The A side now runs the attribute writer over attributes parsed back from stored markdown; the plan must bound this regression explicitly.
findings.answer: Plan 3.4 names the existing carries with a decided block inside A that must stay green as the regression proof, and cites askServerAttributeEqual's []any tolerance and the pure test that already passes a parsed decided block through blockAsItsRowHasIt.

findings.finding: Deleting the three-attribute reading breaks three tests the spec never mentions.
findings.answer: Plan 3.3 names TestCarryVerdict…, TestRowBackedStates… and TestAnswerers… with exactly how each is rewritten, and adds TestAnApprovedVersionsBlocksAreHeldAsTheirRows.

findings.finding: askBlockState/askBlockStateOf survive for N unless replaced; the spec leaves an either/or for the node readers.
findings.answer: Plan section 1: nothing survives - N's blocks travel as model.Ask rows, answerers and carryVerdict read the rows, the RFC 3339 round trip goes; shownAskState/askBlockStates deleted outright; check: grep -rn lists nothing.

findings.finding: An A node whose block id has no row of this document needs a defined answer; a zero-value model.Ask must never reach setAskServerAttributes.
findings.answer: Plan 2.4: heldAsItsRow yields false for a missing row without calling the writer, and the doc comment says why that id cannot decide a carry either way (N refused first if the id stands in N; the still-stands loop refuses if not).

findings.finding: main holds none of the code; the implementer's first act is a base decision (stacked PR on the parent branch, or wait for the merge).
findings.answer: Plan section 5: check #1944; forward-merge main@origin or legion/LEGION-573@origin into the issue branch (jj new with two parents, never a rebase); PR base accordingly; on the parent's merge forward-merge main, retarget, fingerprint, re-run tests.

findings.finding: The repository ships this kind of change with the Envoy CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry and the packages/envoy/AGENTS.md approval bullet, both on the parent branch; and #1944's Fast-follow line names the residual.
findings.answer: Plan section 4: a separate CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased] naming LEGION-752 (right whether or not #1944 ships in the same release), one clause in the AGENTS.md bullet; the parent PR's Fast-follow line is the architect's to strike, named in the completion summary.

findings.finding: Two acceptance bullets are prose judgements (doc comments state A beside N; the node reader's comment says why); the learning bullet needs a command.
findings.answer: Plan 2.7 lists the seven comment sites the reviewer checks as a list; section 4 gives the learning's grep (LEGION-752 present, 'not closed' absent); 6.3 gives the grep that the node readers are gone.

findings.finding: The proof cannot run in the pod as the Surface describes: dev-postgres.sh needs Docker; Dispatch needs pgvector; a skipped Go run is not red.
findings.answer: Plan section 3 (opening) assigns the /tmp Postgres build to the implementer per the LEGION-695 learning, records its coordinates for the tester in the handoff, and states that red-before evidence must show FAIL, not SKIP.

findings.finding: The spec's Problem paragraph reads as if only a document-socket peer reaches the hole; an agent's HTTP reword of a decided block reaches the same A-side hole.
findings.answer: Plan section 9 names it for the architect, who owns the spec's words; the plan's tests and PR body claim the right reach (the wording test and the live HTTP drive).
